idiom_name: sealed trait + case-class nodes with a children method
implementation_notes: A sealed trait with case-class nodes is Scala's direct form of the pattern: each case class declares its node-specific fields and a children member returning the normalized list, generic folds and walks recurse over children, and per-node dispatch is an exhaustive match the compiler checks over the closed hierarchy. Scala 3's enum can declare the same cases with parameters, removing the separate trait. Case classes add structural equality and extractor patterns, which replace the visitor for most analyses; a visitor trait only pays off when operations must be added without touching the node definitions.
pitfalls: Case-class equality recurses through the tree: comparing two large trees is O(tree) and can overflow the JVM stack (use eq or override equals when nodes are tree nodes, not values).
children as a fresh List allocates on every visit; memoise in a lazy val only when the node is immutable.
Deep recursion in walk or eval overflows the JVM stack for large inputs; trampolining or an explicit worklist is needed.
